Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) Module¶

Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) is a powerful, flexible framework for comparing information representations across different modalities, such as between artificial intelligence models and the human brain. Instead of trying to directly map features to brain activity (as in encoding models), RSA asks: “Do two systems represent information in a similar way, i.e., are their ‘neural codes’ or ‘feature spaces’ structurally alike?”

The rsa module within neursen_reveal enables you to perform this high-level comparison. It involves: 1. Computing Representational Dissimilarity Matrices (RDMs): These matrices capture the pairwise “distances” or dissimilarities between representations of different stimuli within a given system (e.g., how different two spoken words are in an AI model’s internal representation, or how different their corresponding brain activation patterns are). 2. Comparing RDMs: The core of RSA is then comparing these RDMs (e.g., using correlation) to quantify the similarity of the representational geometries. A high correlation suggests that the two systems encode information in a structurally similar manner.

This module provides an integrated pipeline for RSA, allowing researchers to gain insights into the correspondence between artificial neural networks and specific brain regions or networks, contributing to our understanding of the computational principles underlying cognition.

Function Reference¶

The primary function for conducting RSA is run_rsa_pipeline.

neursen_reveal.rsa.run_rsa_pipeline(bold_data_root_dir: str, functional_run_name: str, precomputed_features_h5_path: str = None, network_of_interest: str = None, h_delay_trs: int = 2, padding_trs: int = 10, desired_subjects: list = None, perform_statistical_significance_testing: bool = True, extract_features_on_the_fly: bool = False, stimuli_base_path: str = None, tr: float = 2.0, ai_model_id: str = None, ai_layer_name: str = 'final', ai_model_checkpoint: str = None, rsa_metric: str = 'cosine', plot_rdms: bool = True) → tuple[ndarray, ndarray, float][source]¶

Streamlines the RSA pipeline from raw BOLD data to RSA score.

This function handles loading fMRI BOLD data for a specific functional run across multiple subjects, optionally performing statistical voxel selection, applying a network mask, adjusting for hemodynamic delay, filtering padding volumes, and loading/extracting AI features before performing Representational Similarity Analysis.

Parameters¶

bold_data_root_dirstr

Path to the root directory containing BIDS-like fMRI data (e.g., ‘path/to/cifti_analysis’ or ‘data/bids_processed/’).

functional_run_namestr

The common name for the functional run across subjects, corresponding to the task-<label> or task-<label>[_run-<index>] part in BOLD file names. This also serves as the key in your precomputed_features_h5_path (e.g., ‘inamoment’ or ‘coco_run-01’).

precomputed_features_h5_pathstr, optional

Path to the .h5 file containing precomputed AI features, where keys are functional run names. Required if extract_features_on_the_fly is False.

network_of_intereststr, optional

Name of the brain network to parcellate by (e.g., ‘auditory’, ‘language’, ‘visual_A’). If None, RSA will be performed on the entire brain data (after statistical selection if perform_statistical_significance_testing is True).

h_delay_trsint, optional

Hemodynamic delay in TRs. BOLD data will be shifted by this amount. Defaults to 2.

padding_trsint, optional

Number of TRs to remove from the beginning and end of both BOLD and feature data, typically corresponding to silence padding. Defaults to 10.

desired_subjectslist, optional

A list of subject IDs (e.g., [‘sub-UTS01’, ‘sub-UTS02’]) to include in the analysis. If None, all subjects found for the functional_run_name within bold_data_root_dir will be included.

perform_statistical_significance_testingbool, optional

If True, get_significant_voxels_from_arrays will be called to select voxels based on statistical significance across subjects. If False, the mean of BOLD data across subjects will be used (if multiple subjects are involved). Defaults to True.

extract_features_on_the_flybool, optional

If True, features will be extracted using extract_features function. Requires stimuli_base_path, ai_model_id, ai_layer_name. If False, precomputed_features_h5_path must be provided. Defaults to False.

stimuli_base_pathstr, optional

Path to the root directory of your raw stimuli (e.g., ‘data/stimuli/’). Required if extract_features_on_the_fly is True.

trfloat,

The TR (repetition time) duration of your fMRI data in seconds. Required if extract_features_on_the_fly is True for determining how to segment stimuli into TR-aligned features. Defaults to 2.

ai_model_idstr, optional

Identifier for the AI model to use for feature extraction (e.g., ‘whisper’). Required if extract_features_on_the_fly is True.

ai_model_checkpointstr, optional

checkpoint for the AI model to use for feature extraction (e.g., ‘whisper-base’).

ai_layer_namestr, optional

Name of the AI model layer to extract features from. if not specified, final layer’s features will be used.

rsa_metricstr, optional

The distance metric for RSA (e.g., ‘cosine’). Defaults to ‘cosine’.

plot_rdmsbool, optional

If True, plots the computed RDMs. Defaults to True.

Returns¶

tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, float]

A tuple containing: - features_rdm : np.ndarray

The normalized Representational Dissimilarity Matrix (RDM) for the features.

  • bold_rdmnp.ndarray

    The normalized Representational Dissimilarity Matrix (RDM) for the BOLD signals.

  • dist_corrfloat

    The distance correlation coefficient between the two RDMs.

Raises¶

ValueError

If required paths or parameters are missing or invalid.

FileNotFoundError

If BOLD or feature files are not found.

Example Usage¶

This example demonstrates a full RSA pipeline, including on-the-fly feature extraction, for a specific functional run and brain network.

```

from neursen_reveal.rsa import run_rsa_pipeline

import os

# Define placeholder paths for your data

CLEANED_BOLD_ROOT = “/path/to/your/cleaned_bids_data”

RAW_STIMULI_ROOT = “/path/to/your/raw_stimuli_files” # Only needed if extract_features_on_the_fly=True

print(”— Running Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) Pipeline —“)

# Example: Compute RSA for ‘task-storyX’ in the ‘auditory’ network

features_rdm, bold_rdm, rsa_score = run_rsa_pipeline(

bold_data_root_dir=CLEANED_BOLD_ROOT,

functional_run_name=’task-storyX’, # The specific functional run to analyze (e.g., from BIDS file name)

network_of_interest=’auditory’, # Focus RSA on the auditory functional network

h_delay_trs=2, # Hemodynamic delay of 2 TRs

perform_statistical_significance_testing=True, # Perform statistical test

extract_features_on_the_fly=True, # Extract AI features during the RSA run

stimuli_base_path=RAW_STIMULI_ROOT, # Path to your raw stimulus files

ai_model_id=’ecapa-tdnn’, # Specify the AI model for feature extraction

ai_layer_name=’final’, # Layer from which to extract features

tr=2.0, # fMRI TR in seconds

rsa_metric=’cosine’, # Use cosine dissimilarity for RDMs

plot_rdms=True # Generate and display RDM plots

)

print(f”nRSA Results for functional run ‘task-storyX’ in ‘auditory’ network:”)

print(f”Shape of Features RDM: {features_rdm.shape}”)

print(f”Shape of BOLD RDM: {bold_rdm.shape}”)

print(f”Overall RSA Score (correlation between RDMs): {rsa_score:.4f}”)

# The RDM plots will be displayed if plot_rdms is True.

# You can further analyze or save the features_rdm, bold_rdm, and rsa_score.
